current_storage.description: All data access logic in a single monolithic file. Every table's CRUD operations, query construction, and data transformation live here. No repository pattern, no service layer, no abstraction.
current_storage.pattern: Direct Drizzle ORM queries with eq/and/desc operators. Each function maps 1:1 to a route handler. No connection pooling configuration visible. No query caching.

function_categories.operations: getUser, getUserByUsername, createUser, updateUser, getFollowers, getFollowing, followUser, unfollowUser, getUserStats, searchUsers
getPosts, getPost, createPost, updatePost, deletePost, likePost, unlikePost, getPostComments, createComment, deleteComment, likeComment, getTaggedUsers
getCommunities, getCommunity, createCommunity, updateCommunity, getChannels, createChannel

quality_issues: All 77+ functions in a single file -- impossible to test in isolation
No interface/repository abstraction -- routes.ts directly calls storage.ts functions
No error handling patterns -- raw Drizzle errors propagate to route handlers
No query optimization -- no indexes, no pagination strategy, no cursor-based pagination
No connection pooling configuration -- relies on Neon serverless defaults
Denormalized counter updates not atomic -- race conditions on like/comment counts

god_file_splitting.description: Strategy for decomposing the two god files (routes.ts 53KB, storage.ts 105KB) into domain-scoped modules. This is P1 prerequisite before any feature development.

target_modules.description: Registration, login, logout, current user. Will be replaced entirely by Clerk.

Imports all route modules and registers them on the Express app. Single wiring point.

routes_ts.strategy: Extract domain-by-domain starting with the simplest (upload, revenue, notifications) to build confidence, then tackle the large ones (posts, communities, messaging). Each extraction: create module, move routes, update imports in routes/index.ts, verify build, verify runtime.
execution_order: 1. Create server/routes/ directory and index.ts router registry
2. Extract upload.ts (1 route, zero dependencies on other domains)
9. Extract products.ts (5 routes, depends on auth middleware only)
11. Extract communities.ts (10 routes, references channels and messages)
12. Extract messaging.ts (10 routes, references conversations and participants)
13. Extract posts.ts (15 routes, references comments, saves, tags)
14. Extract auth.ts (4 routes, Passport setup -- or skip if Clerk migration is imminent)
routes_ts.risk: MEDIUM -- each extraction can break if imports are wrong or middleware is not forwarded. Must have runtime verification after each step.
routes_ts.prerequisite_for: All new feature development. Cannot add courses, checkout, automations, cross-posting, etc. to a 53KB god file.

target_modules.description: Re-exports all storage functions for backward compatibility during migration.

storage_ts.strategy: Split storage.ts in parallel with routes.ts. Each route module imports from its corresponding storage module. storage/index.ts barrel export preserves backward compatibility until all routes are migrated.
storage_ts.risk: MEDIUM -- shared Drizzle db client import must be consistent. Some functions may have cross-domain dependencies (e.g., createComment updates posts.comments counter).

open_questions.recommendation: Stay with Express. The god file decomposition gives sufficient structure. NestJS migration would be a rewrite with no user-facing benefit.

items.description: Auth bypass: comparePasswords returns true for ALL passwords. Cannot deploy until fixed.
items.resolution: Clerk migration replaces entire auth system

items.description: God file routes.ts (53KB) -- all 89 routes in single file. Blocks parallel development and makes every change risky.
items.resolution: Split into 14 domain modules per god_file_splitting strategy

items.description: God file storage.ts (105KB) -- all 77 data access functions in single file. No abstraction, no testability.
items.resolution: Split into 15 domain modules per god_file_splitting strategy

items.description: No request validation middleware. Raw req.body used everywhere. No Zod schemas on routes despite Zod being in dependencies.
items.resolution: Add Zod validation middleware. Define request/response schemas per route.

items.description: No error handling middleware. Unhandled errors return Express default 500. Some errors leak internal details.
items.resolution: Add centralized error handler that catches all errors and returns structured JSON.

items.description: No rate limiting. Auth endpoints, AI chat, and file upload have no request throttling.
File uploads stored to local filesystem and committed to git. 28 user files in uploads/ directory.
items.resolution: Migrate to S3/R2 object storage. Add uploads/ to .gitignore.

items.description: Hardcoded DELETE /api/force-delete-story/11 route -- dev artifact with hardcoded story ID.
OpenAI client initialized with fallback 'your-api-key' string.
items.resolution: Remove fallback. Require OPENAI_API_KEY env var. Return 503 if not configured.

items.description: No request logging. No way to debug production issues, track response times, or monitor API usage.
items.resolution: Add pino or morgan logging middleware.

items.description: No health check endpoint. Required for Fly.io deployment and monitoring.
items.resolution: Add GET /api/health with database connectivity check.

items.description: WebSocket dependency (ws 8.18.0) installed but no WebSocket server created or used.
items.resolution: Either wire up WebSocket server for real-time features or remove ws dependency.
